title: The School That Changed Its Lost-and-Found
passage:
At the end of every term, Midori School displayed hundreds of lost items on tables near the entrance. Umbrellas, water bottles, towels, pencil cases, and even jackets remained unclaimed. Students were given one week to collect their belongings before many items were donated or discarded. Teachers reminded classes repeatedly, yet the number of unclaimed objects hardly changed.

A student committee decided to study the process. They discovered that the school treated all lost property in the same way. An umbrella found near the gym and a pencil case found in a classroom were both taken to one central room. Students who lost something often did not know when it had been found or where. By the time the large end-of-term display appeared, many students had already replaced small items and stopped looking.

The committee proposed recording found objects with a simple photo and location. Instead of building a new app, they used the school's existing internal website. Staff could upload a picture, select a category, and write where the item had been found. Students could search the page from classroom tablets. Valuable items such as wallets and keys still had to be handled directly by staff and were not photographed publicly.

The first version created too much work. Teachers sometimes spent several minutes describing minor objects. The committee simplified the form to four fields and asked office staff to upload photos only twice a day rather than immediately. They also placed small ‘found item’ boxes in three areas of the school. At fixed times, committee members carried the contents to the office for recording.

After two months, more items were returned within forty-eight hours. Water bottles and pencil cases showed the biggest improvement because students could recognize them quickly from photos. Umbrellas remained difficult because many looked almost identical. The committee added colored tags with temporary numbers when umbrellas were collected, allowing students to compare handles and patterns more carefully.

The end-of-term lost-and-found display did not disappear, but it became much smaller. Teachers spent less time reminding students, and fewer usable items were thrown away. The system succeeded partly because it moved information closer to the time when students still cared about finding the item.

The committee learned that repeated reminders are weak when the underlying process is inconvenient. Students had not ignored lost property because they were careless in every case. Often they lacked enough information to search efficiently. By improving visibility and timing, the school changed behavior without stronger rules. The project also showed that a useful digital system does not need to be complicated. The simplest version that connects the right information with the right person at the right time can be more effective than a feature-rich tool.
translation:
緑中学校では毎学期末、入口近くの机に大量の落とし物が並びました。傘、水筒、タオル、筆箱、上着などが持ち主不明のまま残り、一週間後には寄付や処分の対象になりました。先生が何度呼びかけても数はあまり減りませんでした。

生徒委員会が調べると、学校ではすべての落とし物を同じように中央の一室へ集めていました。体育館近くで見つかった傘も教室の筆箱も同じ場所へ行き、いつどこで見つかったかを生徒が知る方法がほとんどありませんでした。学期末の展示が始まる頃には、小物を買い直して探すのをやめている生徒も多くいました。

そこで、落とし物の写真と発見場所を学校内ウェブサイトへ載せる仕組みを提案しました。新しいアプリは作らず、既存サイトを使い、写真、種類、場所を登録します。財布や鍵などの貴重品は安全上公開せず、職員が直接管理します。

最初の仕組みは入力に時間がかかりすぎたため、項目を四つに減らし、写真登録も一日二回にまとめました。校内三か所に小さな回収箱を置き、委員が決まった時間に職員室へ運ぶようにもしました。

二か月後、特に水筒や筆箱は四十八時間以内に返る割合が増えました。傘は似たものが多いため難しく、回収時に仮番号付きの色タグを付け、柄や持ち手を比べやすくしました。

学期末の展示は完全にはなくなりませんでしたが、量は大きく減りました。先生の呼びかけも少なくなり、使える物の廃棄も減りました。落とし物への関心がまだ残っている早い段階で情報を見せたことが効果につながりました。

委員会は、仕組みそのものが不便なとき、注意喚起だけを繰り返しても効果は弱いと学びました。生徒が必ずしも無責任だったのではなく、効率よく探すための情報が不足していたのです。さらに、役立つデジタル仕組みは複雑である必要もありません。必要な情報を、必要な人へ、必要な時に結び付ける最小限の仕組みが大きな効果を持つことがあります。
